title: Messages, letters, and telling a story
goal: Write short messages, formal letters, and short stories — then use everything you have to talk about your own life.
bekal: write WhatsApp messages in natural spoken Persian
open and close a formal letter correctly
link sentences into a story with connecting words

dialogs.title: گفتگو — پیام‌ها
dialogs.intro: Saturday morning. Budi shows Maryam his phone: he wants to check two messages before sending them.

notes: ⚠️ **Personal messages are written in the spoken form, not the written form.** This surprises many beginners: Iranians write WhatsApp and Telegram messages exactly the way they speak — می‌رم، خوبه، چطوری، دستتون درد نکنه. Writing می‌روم in a message to a friend sounds like reading from a book. Unit 14 isn't just a listening unit; it's a writing unit too.
**"On the contrary" = برعکس**, from بر ("on") + عکس ("image, reverse"). The same word عکس means "photo" — originally a "reversed reflection", which makes sense for a picture.
**"Because of, thanks to" = به خاطرِ**, literally "for the memory of". The word خاطر ("mind, heart") also forms خاطره ("a memory") and به خاطر آوردن ("to remember").

**"I remember" = یادم هست**, literally "my memory is". The same pattern as سرم درد می‌کند in unit 17: the subject isn't the person but the memory. Its opposite: یادم رفت ("I forgot", literally "my memory went").
**"To continue" = ادامه دادن.** Budi's last word in this module, and the word that best closes it.
**Spoken forms in this dialog:** دو تا پیام نوشتم (unchanged), می‌شه نگاه کنین؟ (*mishe negâh konin?*), اولی واسهٔ کیه؟ (*avvali vâse-ye kiye?*), یادم هست (unchanged).

grammars.title: Personal messages: writing the way you speak
after: Notice that almost all of them use **تو**, not شما — messages to friends are always casual. For messages to older people or your boss, switch the endings to the شما form: خوبید؟، کجایید؟، لطف کردید.
**Abbreviations you'll see often:** مرسی (from French), ممنون، فعلاً، بب (from ببخشید), خخخ (laughter, like "lol"). And تشکر is often typed simply as ✌ or 🙏.

grammars.title: Formal letters: openings and closings
after: **The structure of a formal Persian letter is very fixed:** opening → address → body (two to four sentences) → request → closing → name and date. You don't need to invent anything; you only fill in the middle.

با سلام و احترام،
اینجانب بودی سانتوسو، تبعهٔ اندونزی، خواهشمند است ویزایِ مرا تمدید فرمایید. مدارکِ لازم پیوست است.
با تشکر،
بودی سانتوسو

grammars.title: Connecting words for telling a story
after: **With these eight words and the past tense from unit 16, you can already tell any story.** Try it now: write five sentences about yesterday, linked with اول، بعد، چون، and آخرش. That's your first Persian composition.

blocks.text: The following reading uses everything you've learned, and not a single new word outside this module's vocabulary. Read it first without looking at the translation.

head: Persian
Say it
English
rows: سلامِ گرم به مادر و پدرِ عزیزم،
salâm-e garm be mâdar o pedar-e azizam,
Warm greetings to my dear mother and father,
حالِ من خوب است. امیدوارم شما هم خوب باشید.
hâl-e man khub ast. omidvâram shomâ ham khub bâshid.
I'm well. I hope you are well too.
چهار ماه است که در تهران هستم.
chahâr mâh ast ke dar Tehrân hastam.
I've been in Tehran for four months now.
اول خیلی سخت بود، چون هیچ‌کس را نمی‌شناختم.
avval kheyli sakht bud, chon hich-kas râ nemishenâkhtam.
At first it was very hard, because I didn't know anyone.
بعد با یک دوستِ خوب آشنا شدم؛ اسمش مریم است.
ba'd bâ yek dust-e khub âshnâ shodam; esmash Maryam ast.
Then I got to know a good friend; her name is Maryam.
او به من فارسی یاد داد و مرا به خانه‌شان دعوت کرد.
u be man fârsi yâd dâd va marâ be khâneshân da'vat kard.
She taught me Persian and invited me to her home.
ایران‌ها مثلِ ما هستند: مهمان را خیلی دوست دارند.
irânihâ mesl-e mâ hastand: mehmân râ kheyli dust dârand.
Iranians are like us: they love their guests dearly.
هوا اینجا خیلی سرد است و من برف دیدم!
havâ injâ kheyli sard ast va man barf didam!
It's very cold here, and I've seen snow!
God willing, I'll come home in the summer.

blocks.text: Count for yourself: those twelve sentences use the present, the past, the التزامی form, ezafe, را, possessive endings, comparatives, and four connecting words. You have all of it. Four months ago — or twenty units ago — you couldn't read a single one of those sentences.

blocks.title: Three things that will decide the next six months
items: **Don't stop now.** The biggest danger after finishing a beginner module isn't forgetting vocabulary — it's stopping altogether. Fifteen minutes a day for six months beats three hours a day for two weeks, every time.
**Find one person to talk to.** One Persian speaker — a friend, an online tutor, a neighbor — gives you more than ten books. This language was made for the mouth, not for paper.

**Read poetry even before you fully understand it.** Open a verse of Hafez or Saadi now and then. You won't understand all of it, and that's fine. Persian keeps part of its beauty in a place you can only reach through its poetry, and now you have the key to start knocking.
Hi, how are you?
When are you coming?
Sorry I'm late.
Thanks for your help.
I hope you're all well.
